root_cause.text: The memfd_luo preserve function saved the dirty flag of folios at preserve time, but folios could become dirty later (via writes after preserve), causing the serialized state to incorrectly mark them as clean; upon retrieval, the kernel could reclaim these supposedly clean folios under memory pressure, leading to data loss.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The folio might get dirtied later. The serialized state of the folio will mark it as clean. After retrieve, the next kernel will see the folio as clean and might try to reclaim it under memory pressure. This will result in losing user data." The patch removes conditional dirty flag saving and unconditionally sets MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY for all folios.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused variable declaration to improve code cleanliness and avoid compiler warnings.
intent_record.what: Removed the declaration and initialization of an unused variable `unsigned int flags = 0;` inside the for loop in `memfd_luo_preserve_folios()`.
intent_record.how: The change eliminates a local variable that was never referenced in the subsequent code, thereby cleaning up the source without affecting runtime behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unconditionally mark folios as dirty during memfd live update preserve to prevent data loss from reclaim of clean folios that become dirty later.
intent_record.what: Removed conditional setting of MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY flag based on folio_test_dirty, and added unconditional folio_mark_dirty call with explanatory comment.
intent_record.how: The change forces every preserved folio to be marked dirty, preventing the kernel from reclaiming them under memory pressure after a live update, thus avoiding potential data loss from folios that become dirty after the preserve point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY flag by explicitly setting pfolio->flags to include both DIRTY and UPTODATE instead of relying on a potentially incomplete flags variable.
intent_record.what: Removed line that ORed MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_UPTODATE into flags, and replaced pfolio->flags assignment with hardcoded combination of MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY and MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_UPTODATE.
intent_record.how: Previously, pfolio->flags inherited the value of the flags variable which was conditionally set. Now, pfolio->flags is always set to both DIRTY and UPTODATE, ensuring every folio in this path has both flags.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure folios are correctly marked dirty during memfd live update to prevent data loss.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes an unused variable declaration for code cleanliness, which is unrelated to the vulnerability root cause about incorrect dirty flag handling leading to data loss.
The changes directly address the root cause by making the preserve function unconditionally mark folios as dirty, preventing data loss from reclaim of folios that become dirty after preservation.

candidates.rationale: The condition selectively saves the dirty flag only if the folio is currently dirty, failing to account for folios that become dirty later via writes after preserve, leading to data loss when the kernel reclaims incorrectly marked clean folios.

This statement is executed only when the condition on line 157 is true, so if the folio is not dirty at preservation time, the dirty flag is not set, causing the serialized state to incorrectly mark the folio as clean.

The assignment stores the flags value, which may lack the MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY flag if the folio was not dirty at preservation time, thereby persisting the incomplete state that leads to data loss upon reclaim.
